requirement: A Joomla import that cannot install Claude Cowork keeps each road's evidence and names the host limit (memory, upload size) instead of a bare install_failed

oracle.ref: PR #1498 (fix); fix evidence: Joomla 6.1.3 with memory_limit 128M and upload/post limits 8M, ~60 MB package (19/10/2026): the URL install POST died with a 500 (memory exhausted), the upload came back 200 with nothing installed, and the diagnostic kept only the later 200
oracle.invariant: S1: reason upload_too_large; no upload POST is sent; diagnostic.roads.url_install.post_status is 500 and roads.upload_install.cause is over_limit; php_limits and package_bytes are kept. S2: reason site_resource_limit with check memory_exhausted; no page text is kept in the diagnostic. S3: the upload is sent and the result is install_failed, its diagnostic carrying both roads. S4: the result is ok. S5: only known road names, causes and limit names survive; the alert shows a Roads line and a Sizes line. S6: a package 8 KB under an 8M post_max_size is still uploaded; a 100 KB first chunk starting with the memory error is still read; a failed download after a URL memory error is site_resource_limit; a 403 on the upload then a URL 500 keeps both roads, the limits and the 403.
oracle.productSourcesScope: file-level: the files the case imports, reads or runs (declaration line, or the first code line); the invariant is exercised through them, the executed assertion is the case command

writes: run dir under QA_ARTIFACT_ROOT: logs/, tmp/<case> (the child TMPDIR, removed after the run)

assertionIds: a URL 500 then a package over the known upload limits is upload_too_large, the 500 kept
a POST whose answer carries PHP memory exhaustion is site_resource_limit
limits phpinfo does not show change nothing: the upload is sent and its failure is install_failed
an upload that lands is a success, and the URL road that would die is never asked
a package under the known limits still goes over the upload road
phpinfo limits are read as PHP reads them: K, M, G, -1, and unknown when missing
an install stopped by a host limit names the limit, not "install it yourself"
a package just under post_max_size is still sent: the envelope counted is the real one
PHP's memory error at the head of a large first chunk is still read
a package that cannot be downloaded after a URL memory error is site_resource_limit
a 403 on the upload then a URL 500 keeps both roads, the PHP limits and the 403
